title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Avery Chen
summary: Authoritative People Ops playbook and manager guide covering hiring workflow, interview scorecards, offer and acceptance timelines, 90-day onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, and manager responsibilities.
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document codifies Redwood Inference’s People Ops standards for hiring, new-employee onboarding, performance reviews, feedback cycles, and the core manager responsibilities that ensure consistent, equitable employee experiences. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and engineering managers.

Scope: Individual contributors and managers across all teams (engineering, product, research, go-to-market). Excludes executive compensation, legal agreements, and external contractor engagement (see finance-and-legal for those processes).

Key principles
- Candidate experience: respectful, timely, and transparent communication.
- Equity and fairness: structured scorecards, diverse panels, and consistent evaluation rubrics.
- Manager responsibility: managers are accountable for hiring decisions, onboarding plans, and performance coaching.
- Data-driven: time-to-fill, offer-accept rates, new hire ramp metrics, and review calibration recorded and reported monthly.

Hiring process (end-to-end)

Goals and SLAs
- Target time-to-fill: 30 calendar days from job posting to offer.
- Interview-to-offer SLA: 14 days from first onsight to final interview debrief.
- Offer acceptance window: standard is 48 hours (exceptions require people-ops approval).
- Target candidate response time between steps: 48 business hours.

Roles and responsibilities
- Hiring manager: defines role spec, interview plan, final decision, and onboarding plan.
- Recruiter: sources candidates, coordinates interviews, negotiates offers, and tracks pipeline metrics.
- Interviewers: prepare using scorecard, submit feedback within 24 hours.
- People Ops: approves final offer package, ensures equity checks, and executes background checks and I-9 processing.

Standard interview stages
1. Recruiter screen (30–45 min): role fit, basic qualifications, compensation band alignment.
2. Hiring manager screen (30–45 min): scope, expectations, culture fit.
3. Technical/skills loop (2–4 interviews, up to 3 hours total): role-appropriate assessments.
4. Cross-functional or leadership interview (as needed).
5. Debrief and final decision (hiring manager synthesizes feedback; people-ops consulted for equity/comp basis).

Interview scorecard (required for every candidate in interview loop)
- Fields (all required): role, interviewer, date, technical competency (1–5), problem solving (1–5), communication (1–5), collaboration/culture fit (1–5), ownership & impact (1–5), notes (free text), overall recommendation (strong hire / hire / no hire / hold).
- Scoring guidance: 1 = does not meet bar, 3 = meets expectations, 5 = significantly exceeds bar.

Diversity & fairness checklist (must be completed before extending an offer)
- Panel diversity: at least one interviewer from a different team or background when possible.
- Consistent questions: ask the same core role-specific questions to all candidates in the same cohort.
- Compensation parity check: people-ops verifies band placement against peers.

Offer and negotiation
- Standard offer components: role title, level, base salary, target bonus (if applicable), equity units (where applicable), benefits summary, start date, hiring manager contact, and relocation/hybrid policy.
- Standard acceptance window: 48 hours. For counteroffers or complex signings give an additional 24–48 hours at people-ops discretion.
- Compensation approvals: offers above band midpoint or any exceptions require people-ops + hiring manager director approval.

Background checks & preboarding
- Trigger: contingent offer acceptance. People Ops will order background check and I-9.
- Preboarding checklist (to be run by hiring manager + recruiter):
  - Workspace and laptop order placed (IT ticket)
  - Slack, Google (or corporate SSO) account created
  - Calendar invites for Day 1 orientation, 30/60/90 check-ins
  - Access to team repos, docs, and runbooks provisioned
  - Manager’s 90-day onboarding plan shared

Employee onboarding: 0–90 day playbook

Pre-boarding (before Day 1)
- People Ops & IT complete account provisioning and any hardware shipments 3–5 business days before start.
- Hiring manager sends a welcome email with start logistics, team org snapshot, and first-week agenda.

Day 1 (orientation)
- 09:00–10:30: Company orientation (People Ops): benefits, payroll, security, code of conduct.
- 10:45–12:00: Team welcome (hiring manager): role expectations, immediate priorities, team norms.
- Afternoon: workspace setup, required compliance training, buddy introduction.

Week 1
- Shadow sessions with cross-functional partners.
- Complete mandatory trainings (security, data handling) and access provisioning.
- Deliverable: first-week summary email from new hire to manager listing questions and immediate blockers.

30/60/90 day structure (manager checklist)
- 30-day: Confirm access, small deliverable completed, initial feedback meeting, set 90-day objectives.
- 60-day: Review progress on objectives, identify blockers, update development goals, consider stretch assignment.
- 90-day: Formal probation review (if applicable), performance summary, confirm long-term goals, and decide on role adjustments.

New manager onboarding (first 30 days)
- Required: Manager onboarding course (People Ops), 1:1 cadence set-up, HR policies review, direct reports introductory meetings scheduled.

Performance & feedback cycles

Cadence and types of feedback
- Continuous feedback: encouraged via 1:1s, Slack praise, and documented comments in performance system.
- Formal reviews: twice annually (mid-year and end-of-year) plus a 90-day new-hire review.
- Calibration panels: once per review cycle by leadership to align ratings and compensation changes.

Review process (biannual)
1. Self-review: employee completes a structured self-assessment (strengths, accomplishments, goals, development areas). Deadline: 10 business days before manager review window closes.
2. Manager review: manager completes assessment including examples and proposed rating.
3. Upward manager peer feedback: cross-team input collected for leadership roles.
4. Calibration: HR/People Ops + managers discuss distribution, adjust for consistency.
5. Rating & compensation recommendation: people-ops approves final comp changes.
6. One-on-one meeting: manager reviews results and development plan with employee within 5 business days of finalization.

Rating scale and definitions (common language)
- Exceeds expectations: consistently over-delivers and creates measurable impact.
- Meets expectations: reliably delivers on core responsibilities.
- Needs improvement: performance gaps requiring defined improvement plan.

Performance improvement plans (PIP)
- Trigger: consistent rating of Needs improvement or major single-incident performance problem.
- Steps: document gap, set measurable objectives and timeline (typically 60–90 days), weekly manager check-ins, People Ops oversight, end-of-plan review.
- Outcome: remove plan (performance sufficient), extend (rare, with People Ops), or termination. All PIPs require People Ops review and legal involvement for high-risk cases.

Manager responsibilities (practical checklist)
- Hiring: write clear role spec, curate interview panel, ensure scorecards are used, and make final recommendation with documented rationale.
- Onboarding: provide 90-day plan, schedule training/meetings, assign buddy, and complete 30/60/90 check-ins.
- Growth & career conversations: set yearly objectives, run career ladder conversations twice a year, sponsor high performers.
- Feedback: provide frequent, timely, and documented feedback; escalate unresolved issues to People Ops.
- Promotions: own calibration packet, write promotion rationale, collect evidence and peer feedback, and submit to people-ops for review.

Manager checklist before leaving the company
- Handover of direct reports: 1) document status of all direct reports, 2) schedule introduction meeting with interim manager, 3) update performance notes in system.

Operational metrics & reporting
- People Ops tracks: time-to-fill, offer-accept rate, new-hire retention at 90/180/365 days, manager satisfaction with recruiter support, diversity metrics by funnel stage.
- Monthly report owners: People Ops maintains the dashboard; hiring managers receive team-specific metrics quarterly.

Compliance & security
- Mandatory trainings: security awareness, data handling, and code of conduct completed within first 14 days.
- Access provisioning: least-privilege principle; managers must request elevated entitlements with justification and review every 90 days.

Escalation paths
- Hiring disagreements: final decision rests with hiring manager; people-ops can escalate to manager’s director for unresolved edge cases.
- Performance disputes: initiate mediation with People Ops; if unresolved, escalate to HR Business Partner and Legal for high-risk matters.

Appendix: Quick checklists
- Hiring manager quick checklist: role spec, panel, scorecards, compensation band check, offer approval, onboarding plan.
- Recruiter quick checklist: sourcing plan, candidate comms, interview scheduling, offer paperwork, preboarding items.
- New hire first-week checklist: orientation, 1:1 with manager, buddy pairings, system access, required training.

Document ownership & review cadence
- Owner: People Ops.
- Review cadence: annual review or earlier if policy/regulatory change required.
- Contact: people-ops@redwood-inference.internal for questions or exception requests.
